new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened (5 pp., text, the PDF's metadata: 'Microsoft Word - Mesem.rtf', Distiller Dec 2009). extracted text gives, under the heading 'Suprasegmentals (tone, stress, length)' on the page footed 'Mesem (Mesẽ Momolili) OPD Printed: December 3, 2009 Page 3': "We find non-contrastive stress in Mesẽ, exhibiting word initial primary stress, with secondary stress on subsequent alternating syllables, optionally occurring in the ultimate position on words of three syllables or more in length." Byte-for-byte identical to the reported quote (the text encodes Mesẽ as e + combining tilde U+0303). It is the entire suprasegmentals section: one sentence, no stress-marked examples, no tone or length remarks;…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Stress is not contrastive. Primary stress falls on the first syllable of the word; secondary stresses fall on alternating syllables after it (i.e., a left-to-right trochaic pattern), and in words of three or more syllables a secondary stress may optionally land on the final syllable.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Secondary stress on subsequent alternating syllables (3rd, 5th..); optionally on the ultimate syllable in words of three or more syllables.
new_statements.exceptions: None stated; the only variation noted is the optional final-syllable secondary stress in 3+-syllable words. No examples with stress marked are given; the recorded text is not stress-marked.
new_statements.domain_note: Word level ('word initial primary stress'); the OPD is a 5-page SIL organised-phonology-data sheet, based on elicited words; no tone or length reported under the 'Suprasegmentals (tone, stress, length)' heading. SIL catalogue lists author as unknown; Glottolog/SIL-PNG bibliography attributes it to Kathy Vanaria. The OPD's bibliography cites an earlier Burns, Gail 1990 'Mese: organized phonology data paper' (ms., SIL Ukarumpa) which this 2002 sheet updates.
new_statements.identity_note: The source calls the language 'Mesem (Mese, Momolili) Language [MCI]' / 'Mesẽ', villages Samanzing, Tuzing, Hobu, Lae area, Morobe Province — this is mese1244 itself, not a dialect. Note the OPD is an SIL organised-phonology-data sheet (5 pp.), catalogued at SIL as 'Author unknown' but attributed to Kathy Vanaria in the SIL-PNG bibliography used by Glottolog (ref 23669).
